review_notes:
I reviewed all of lines 1–43, which hold six declarations: boundedQ_triangulated, quotientEvaluationAdditive, quotientEvaluationLifting, quotientEvaluationShift, quotientEvaluationFactorsShift and quotientEvaluationTriangulated. I also read the definitions they depend on: boundedQuotientEvaluation and boundedQuotientEvaluationFactors in BoundedQuotientEvaluation.lean, and quotientEvaluation and quotientEvaluationFactors in ThickEvaluation.lean. For comparison I read the matching Mathlib code: Localization.functor_additive_iff (CalculusOfFractions/Preadditive.lean), Localization.essSurj_mapArrow (CalculusOfFractions.lean; this is a lemma, not an instance), Functor.isTriangulated_of_precomp_iso (Triangulated/Functor.lean), and the derived-category pattern in Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/ExactFunctor.lean and Localization/Triangulated.lean.

Every proof in the file already follows the standard Mathlib pattern:
- The additivity proof is a `rw [Localization.functor_additive_iff ...]` followed by `exact Functor.additive_of_iso ...`. This is exactly how Localization/Triangulated.lean proves its additivity results.
- The Lifting, CommShift and NatTrans.CommShift instances copy the ExactFunctor.lean construction for `F.mapDerivedCategory`, including the `inferInstanceAs (NatTrans.CommShift (Lifting.iso ...).hom ℤ)` step.
- The IsTriangulated instance has to supply `mapArrow.EssSurj` as a local `have`. That is because `Localization.essSurj_mapArrow` is a lemma rather than a global instance for `W.Q`. After that, one call to `isTriangulated_of_precomp_iso` finishes the proof.
- `boundedQ_triangulated` is just `inferInstance`.

None of these proofs has a redundant step, an unnecessary case split, or a better-named lemma it could use instead. Rewriting the additivity proof as a term using `.mpr` would only be a change of style, so under the rubric I did not report it. One thing I could not check: since I can't run Lean, I don't know whether the local `have` in quotientEvaluationTriangulated could be dropped because some instance in the OAI library already provides it. I found no source evidence of such an instance.
